purpose: Every article or resource of a blog or a resource hub as one ruled list, with the controls to narrow it on one row. `filters` picks the filter bar: `category-search` draws a category picker and a search field (the blog), `facets` draws one dropdown per facet — content type, category, industry — that wraps when it runs out of room (a resource hub). Each entry is a row — its cover on the left, and on the right its overline, headline, a deck and, when it has them, its writers with the byline; the row is one link named by its headline, and from `lg` up a read cue rises into its end on hover or keyboard focus. The filters combine; a facet dropdown with more than seven options gains an option search; a load-more button reveals the next page, and when nothing matches an empty state offers to clear every filter. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'article-index', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `frame-box`, `toggle-group`, `select`, `input`, `avatar`, `empty-state` and `button`; the selected category, the search term, the facet selections, each dropdown's option search and the page count are local state. A row without a cover draws its client's mark in one flat ink that follows the theme.
useWhen: Use ArticleIndex for the full filterable list of articles or resources; choose the filter bar with `filters`: `category-search` for the blog (category picker and search field), `facets` for a resource hub (one dropdown per facet).
avoidWhen: For a card grid of customer stories with search and facets → use `story-library`.
For a filterable list of non-article rows (jobs) → use `listing-browser`.
For a closing row of related articles → use `article-cards`.
related: article-highlight` — the band that opens the blog above this list.
story-library` — the card-grid library with search and facets.
listing-browser` — the filterable list of job rows.
bestPractices: With `filters="category-search"`, list the articles newest first and file every article under at least one of `categories`; keep the category list short enough to scroll on one row.

With `filters="facets"`, give every item a `facets` entry per facet `id` it can be filtered by (an item without one never matches a selection on that facet), and keep each facet's `options` to values some item carries.
Set `emptyTitle` (and `emptyActionLabel`) so a reader who filters everything away gets a way back; without it the list just disappears.
Set `leading` to the number of entries a highlight band above already shows, so they are not listed twice until the reader filters.
Leave `rowVariant` unset to get the layout that fits the filter bar: `byline` for `category-search`, `center` for `facets`.
